title: Amodei calls for slowdown and invites audits, Altman delays IPO for safety concerns - TCR 09/13/26
description:
Anthropic's CEO published a "We Must Pace the Frontier" essay urging an industry slowdown and pledged permanent outside-evaluator access, OpenAI's Sam Altman called a 2026 IPO "ill-advised" over safety, and a bipartisan Senate bill from Thune, Cruz, and Klobuchar would impose a legal "duty of care" on frontier AI developers and let the federal government ask a federal court to block the release of certain models deemed unsafe.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-september-13-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:59 Anthropic urges a slowdown, OpenAI delays its IPO
4:12 Senate bill turns safety pledges into a duty of care
6:34 AI finds hidden cell-bridge proteins
9:15 One injection edits most of a mouse liver
12:00 xAI assembles the nation's biggest battery
15:35 Close

This episode covers the Anthropic slowdown call and Hugging Face's bid to join its evaluator program, Sam Altman's comments on a 2026 IPO, the Senate duty-of-care bill and potential preemption of relevant provisions in California and Illinois AI laws, an AI search of 214 million protein shapes that found the TM184C cell-bridge receptor, a Wuhan University guide-RNA advance reaching 70 percent prime editing in mouse liver, and xAI's 3.3-gigawatt-hour Memphis battery beside a 30-rollback EPA pollution report.

On Saturday, September 12, Anthropic's chief executive published "We Must Pace the Frontier," urging the industry to slow how fast it makes models more capable and pledging permanent, employee-level access for third-party evaluators to inspect Anthropic's systems. Hours later, OpenAI's Sam Altman called a 2026 IPO "ill-advised" over safety, conceded an AI beyond human control is "absolutely" possible, and hinted that an industry pacing agreement might be close, while Elon Musk answered the essay with three words: "Dario is right." A bipartisan Senate draft from Thune, Cruz, and Klobuchar would impose a binding duty of care on frontier developers, require covered frontier models to undergo testing by national-laboratory scientists, and let the federal government ask a federal court to block certain model releases deemed unsafe, alongside a clause that would potentially preempt relevant provisions of California's and Illinois's stronger state laws. In the lab, researchers compared the shapes of more than 214 million predicted proteins and surfaced TM184C, a receptor cells use to build bridges and pass each other fuel, cargo, and whole mitochondria, while a Wuhan University team armored a guide RNA end to end and reached close to 70 percent editing in a mouse liver from one injection. And near Memphis, xAI assembled what executives call the nation's biggest battery, 3.3 gigawatt-hours of storage, as more than 800 former EPA officials warned that thirty pollution-rule rollbacks could contribute to 1,300 premature deaths by 2028. The thread through all of it: the ability to check these systems is moving into many hands at once.
